# Retained sparse cell audit

Source audited: release-1019/src-8b08b0bbf31394f4e626e6ca7192af6bc3e556b718b4472435e3e161f78652fe, protocol 50. Read-only source audit. No compiled prototype, GPU work, production edits, or performance claim.

## Decision

A retained stable index is technically sound, but postpone implementation until the current actual-app performance and fragment candidates are measured. The existing resolve-sol conclusion reports only about 0.30 ms saved in render stages by resolving once, with about 0.24 ms of added compute/barrier residual. It does not establish several milliseconds of removable vertex cost. Retained metadata avoids compute each frame, but introduces index reads, segment selection, update complexity and memory. A source-only implementation now would duplicate large renderer changes without measurement evidence.

## Exact static eligibility

The current tile_vs maps instance to local_cell and layer, then resolve_sprite rejects hidden layers/categories, invalid wrap/cull, out-of-LUT values, ZERO_EMPTY values and sets with zero frames. Classify only the latter three value/set properties as retained nonempty metadata. Decode raw values with tile_render_shared::layer_value, including palette_shift, before checking lut_len and ZERO_EMPTY. Resolve the LUT entry, then check the set header's frame count. A nonzero raw palette value does not imply a nonzero sprite value.

Do not test the currently selected frame, sprite alpha bounds, downscaled sprite, atlas content, camera category, camera cull or per-cell offsets during static classification. Keeping those tests in the existing shader preserves phase changes, animations with blank frames, atlas swaps, clean-map filtering and offsets without camera-specific metadata. LAYER_HIDDEN could be removed statically because same_shape includes it, but the narrow design leaves all visibility tests unchanged.

## Concrete retained candidate

For each active binding and pass, retain rows of live records sorted by physical world column, then original layer index. Each GPU live record is one u32 encoding cell_index * pass.count + relative_layer. Checked arithmetic must reject overflowing encodings and use dense fallback. CPU metadata retains each row's prefix count at column boundaries. It does not retain rendered pixels, sprite geometry, phases or offsets. World values remain in the current packed tile buffer.

At draw encoding, intersect the existing visible window with world rows. Wrap or reject rows exactly as wrap_cell does. Split each row's horizontal sequence at world wrap boundaries, retaining every repeated copy if the viewport spans multiple world periods. Respect params.descending. Produce small segments containing prefix instance end, live-record interval, direction, unwrapped origin adjustment, and original local row/column mapping. Empty segments disappear. Segment order follows the original local row, local column and layer sequence. Work on a frame is proportional to visible rows and wrap segments, not world cells or cell-layer pairs.

Upload these bounded controls through existing control-slot lifetime management. Draw one indexed instance stream per pass. The vertex shader binary-searches segment ends, selects the live record, reconstructs the exact original local_cell/layer pair, then calls the existing resolve_sprite and geometry path unchanged. Descending segments must reverse CELL GROUPS only. Reversing individual live records would reverse layers within each cell and break painter order. A descending row therefore needs its own row list, or prefix/rank lookup selecting the preceding cell followed by ascending layer rank. Start the narrow prototype with a second descending list only for passes that actually descend; account for its full bytes.

Use a cell-only bind group replacing binding 7, which tile vertices do not use, for compact metadata. Preserve the original group for free sprites. This matches the eight vertex-storage-binding limit and avoids moving the tile-data tail when slot capacity grows. Segment controls can share this buffer only in separately bounded slot-owned ranges. No new device feature, indirect support, compute dispatch, readback or fence is needed.

The CPU prefix representation requires O(binding_count * cell_count * pass_count) counters, and GPU records require 4 * nonempty_count bytes, plus descending copies. This is unacceptable without an explicit budget. Do not allocate for all theoretical bindings. Admit only active binding/pass caches and cap aggregate CPU metadata, GPU metadata, active plus retired capacity, and controls. Dense fallback is mandatory when a cap or checked arithmetic fails. An admitted world's camera movements must not trigger full-world cache rebuilding. A new binding may stay dense until its bounded metadata preparation completes.

## Update and invalidation contract

set_world builds or declines admitted caches. same_shape already compares sets, LUTs, palette/index bits, pass order, categories, phase/offset layout and other layer specs, so changes to these reach full set_world. sync_tables handles slot allocation/free and binding changes without same_shape failing; therefore this path must explicitly invalidate/rebuild affected binding/pass rows before publishing new compact controls. Never key solely by world shape or default layer data. Dirty Records are region/cell pairs, including slot regions. Map each changed region to affected bindings and the owning layer/pass. Only rebuild affected row lists and column prefix counts, then update their GPU ranges. Dirty All may rebuild caches once on world mutation. Dirty None/update_free must not scan cells. Phase-only or offset-only records may cause bounded row work but cannot change eligibility.

Rows need reserved capacity or an admitted bounded allocator so one insertion does not shift the entire world list. Holes are fine if the row directory and segment controls select the new row interval. Retire old ranges according to existing queue/control completion. CPU packing must never overwrite controls referenced by outstanding slots. GPU queue ordering protects data update/read order, but does not permit unbounded allocations while previous buffers remain alive. A row update that cannot be admitted falls back to dense for the affected pass until safe publication. Atlas swaps do not invalidate static eligibility; shader resolution still reads current sprite metadata.

## Independent acceptance gates

1. Enumerate the baseline instance sequence independently on CPU, with cell, unwrapped coordinates, layer, binding and selected set/frame. Filter only the exact static eligibility predicate. Compare it entry-for-entry with compact reconstruction. Include empty/full/random rows, multiple layers per cell, descending rows, negative wrap coordinates, both-axis wrap, repeated world periods, nonwrapping edges and palette-only raw values. This proves ordering independently of matching final pixels.
2. Run GPU exact-image comparisons against unchanged renderer, including retained real-art matrix, all animation phases, blank/nonblank frame alternation, alternate data-slot bindings, clean-map categories, cull offsets, per-cell offsets beyond anchors, scale/invert blends, downscale twins, atlas replacement and incremental atlas metadata changes. Overlapping translucent sprites on consecutive cells/layers must make a reorder visibly fail.
3. Apply insert/delete dirty sequences, slot allocate/free/rebind and Dirty All. After every operation compare retained lists and prefixes against a fresh independent reconstruction. A world with Dirty None and moving cameras must report zero eligibility rescans and zero world metadata writes.
4. Force every metadata/control admission cap and buffer-growth boundary while all existing control slots are in flight. Check dense output equality and measured active-plus-retired bytes. No waits, locks, unsafe, readbacks, global per-frame scans or pixel rendering on CPU are permitted.
5. Only after these gates, compare matched current-app native 4K 240 Hz camera traces with forced whole frames. Report CPU frame preparation/encode/submit, GPU whole-frame and per-pass p50/p95/p99, cache bytes, live/dense instance counts, metadata updates and fallback counts. Require repeatable frame-time gain without tail regression. Never treat the historical resolve timing as current performance qualification.

Relevant source locations: tile-render-shaders/src/lib.rs resolve_sprite and tile_vs; tile-render/src/renderer.rs WorldBuffers::same_shape, set_world, sync_tables, update_cells and Steps::draw; tile-render-shared/src/lib.rs layer_value, window_col and wrap_cell. The existing resolve-sol/compaction-plan.md is a different GPU per-frame block-compaction design. This proposal specifically avoids that per-frame resolution/compute pass.
